Manius raced in a frenzy towards the clearing. He was so close. He was about to unleash the swarm when a breach in the heavens shook Gaea's core.

The infinite one took its representation on the mortal plane, and as it left it took Manius's swarm with it.

If Manius had a jaw, it would have dropped. Such an event occurring at such a critical moment seemed extraordinarily unlikely.

With no other options, Manius wandered into the clearing and issued a challenge.

"Whoever runs this pitiful village, I, Manius, challenge you for the right to rule this clan."

*****

Luminus was utterly confounded by the recent turn of events. It would appear, at the very least, that the gods had a very strange, twisted sense of humour. It seems that the divinities would have him win this war, that much seemed certain. A mild anger sparked within his being. The mortals are to decide their own destiny, why else would there be a need for mortals. Why grant sentience at all when events are doomed to fall. So when the challenge came, Luminus found it a relief. Perhaps there was still a way to test his convictions, to divine the true path of the spectra. Manius has issued a challenge. Luminus would accept, if only to assuage his own doubts.

"I am Luminus, de facto leader of the Forest Spectra, and I accept your challenge."

As Luminus walked into the open to greet his opponent, Manius sent a wild cry, lifted a wicked blade, and charged.

*****

Luminus cringed as a looping overhead swing landed shortly where he stood before. As the battle dragged on, Manius's attacks became more frenzied, more erratic and wild. "Such, " Luminus thought, "is the way of force."

Luminus continued to observe, everytime as Manius prepared to swing, he would impart the slightest smidgen of hesitation, expanding his opponent's growing uncertainty in his own strength.

"Your attacks are futile, you'll never strike me." Luminus observed. His observation was only met with a bestial cry from his opponent.

"Don't you see it Manius," Luminus ducked, and the greatsword passed cleanly through the air which his head had occupied mere moments before, "The error of your ways?"

"Force is insufficient, true power lies in knowledge and understanding. To see where your opponents tread, nay, to decide where your opponent treads. Every swing you make is because I allow it." Luminus spoke, and with it he shared a vision, a vision of a brighter future for the spectra, away from the looming threat of war.

Manius hesitated, then began to raise his sword.

So Luminus acted, without hesitation. If Manius would not listen, then he would be made to listen. With absolute determination, Luminus directed a beam of moonlight right onto Manius's sword arm.

"It doesn't have to end this way you know, Psychos' gift is one to be cherished, to be given to the deserving and the lost. To deliver it to the masses is to diminish its value. Take my hand Manius, you have great gifts, and if you could learn moderation then we could accomplish much together."

The cries fell on deaf ears. Manius stared blankly, an intense hatred radiating outwards. It was too late, it had always been too late. His hunger and anger had consumed him.

Luminus picked up the greatsword, and pierced Manius's core with one swift strike. Suddenly, Manius was no more.

It was the miracle of a new beginning, a new dawn for the spectra, as they finally stood united as one people.

Yet even as the New Dawn arrived for the spectra, Luminus felt that something had already been lost.

Phyra was pleased with the spectacle.
